answer: New agents enter on probation: each starts with a tiny transaction cap, like a cedar seedling, and the cap only grows after a trail of completed jobs confirmed by independent counterparties. A sybil swarm faces a real cost - every fake identity must slowly earn its own history, and one confirmed fraud marks the whole cluster with an umber stain on the public ledger, freezing its caps. Honest work creates a ripple: each verified job raises the cap a little and vouches for the next, so reputation compounds only for agents that actually deliver, while cheap copies stay small forever.
